articles.title: They took a robot baby home for the weekend. By Monday, their testosterone responded differently
articles.summary: Childless couples who cared for a lifelike baby doll showed no testosterone change at first, but after a weekend with the doll at home, men’s and women’s levels fell by about 9 to 12 percent during joint caregiving.

articles.title: A bigger paycheck tends to come with personality changes, according to a large-scale analysis of psychology research
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 11 long-running studies covering up to 134,515 workers found that rising pay tended to precede small gains in conscientiousness and emotional stability, along with slight drops in agreeableness and extraversion.

articles.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
articles.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease. The strongest benefits appeared at 5,000 to 7,500 daily steps, suggesting that the popular 10,000-step goal may not be necessary.

articles.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup. The findings reveal a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could pave the way for treatments that mimic this natural defense.

articles.title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
articles.summary: A discovery in tiny algae led to a Nobel Prize-winning breakthrough that allows scientists to switch brain cells on and off using light. The revolutionary technique has already helped researchers activate memories and is opening new possibilities for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.

articles.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain. By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

articles.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions. The workflow combines reference retrieval and contrastive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) evidence with reference-based LLM reasoning and deterministic validation. Experiments on a test dataset show that the workflow produces more consistent, evidence-grounded and traceable diagnoses than the same LLM without structured workflow guidance.

articles.title: What Social Media Teaches Us About Accumulative AI Risks
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.24006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prominent AI safety discussions emphasize existential threats and catastrophic events, such as AI-enabled nuclear conflict or engineered biological outbreaks. This position paper argues that there is another type of AI risk that arises and accumulates from the widespread use of AI. Drawing on lessons from social media, we argue that safety assessments must also address accumulative harms that develop through repeated use, recurring decisions, and feedback across interconnected deployments. articles.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels
